study: Independent participant replication of the frozen sub-04 four-trial encoder and equal-weight Fisher classifier on personal12. Each participant supplies four physical trials per photograph. The participants have distinct EEG; their two menus may share photographs.
stage_at_registration: Known sub-04 mixed 65/120 versus Fisher 53/120, trial-only 58. Known Fisher counts for sub-05 and sub-01 (56 and 52). No trial-head predictions or outcomes on either replication target menu inspected. The support design and original Fisher renderings were already used.
training: Independently initialize and train each participant on the identical ordered 512 generic objects with only their own EEG. Use exact original fit, training-only mean and SD, 63 x 125 samples from four physical trials in recorded order; seed 260553, default initialization, one final fit of 750 updates. No sub-04 weights, early stopping, tuning, participant selection, gate or retraining.
classification: For each participant only, unchanged 17-channel 96D Fisher and four-trial 96D encoder; for each query normalize prototype cosine scores across the existing 12-word menu exactly as in sub-04. Primary 50:50 arithmetic average. Each object and fold supplies its eight calibrated photos, excluding both held-out photos. Separate pure-encoder diagnostic. All 12 objects per person in one recording-session pair.
generation: Per participant reproduce all old Fisher word decisions and H14 visual conditions; unchanged native H14 prior/residual angle, radius, generator, seed 923761+original row. Only change predicted word and consequent existing support set. Own/uniform/same-predicted-word and fold donor; singleton self. Render all 120 rows x 3 arms for each participant irrespective of score. No original query images in predictions or rendering.
analysis: Report hits, paired gains/losses and object-bootstrap intervals separately per person with 10000 draws, seed 260552. Report both outcomes whether positive or negative. Pooled supplementary intervals must keep shared object identity across participants. Same predeclared generated-image naming/CLIP, DINO within-ten, strict assignment and controls as in sub-04. No participant-population generalization.
